betterarrows.config.title: Better Arrows
betterarrows.config.stuckArrows.tooltip: Draw arrows at their real hit point, following the bone they hit. Turn off for vanilla placement.
betterarrows.config.stickThroughInvulner: Off by default. Vanilla refuses damage for a second after a hit and bounces the arrow off. Turning this on makes it stick instead - but it deals no damage, so the arrow is showing a hit that did not land.
betterarrows.config.surfaceSounds.toolti: Wood thuds, stone clacks, metal rings. Blocks that make their own noise (bells, amethyst) are left alone.
Deliberately quiet: meant to be noticed up close, not announced across the area.
betterarrows.config.blockParticles.toolt: Crumble particles carrying the real texture of the block that was hit.
betterarrows.config.ricochet.tooltip: Glancing shots skip off hard surfaces. Gameplay change - on a server it is the server's setting that counts.
betterarrows.config.ricochetAngle.toolti: Measured from the surface: 0 slides along the wall, 90 is straight into it. Only shallower hits bounce, so a head-on shot still sticks. The material narrows it further: wood takes about half of this, loose ground like sand, gravel or dirt only a sliver near flat, and wool, mud or snow never bounce at all.
betterarrows.config.ricochetEnergy.toolt: This is the MOST an arrow keeps, on a hit travelling flat along the surface. The steeper the shot the less is left to leave with - the same rule as bouncing off ice - and the material takes its own share on top: stone gives back all of this, wood a little over half, loose ground like sand or gravel four fifths of it, but only ever at the near-flat angle it lets bounce at all. Higher values send arrows skipping further. Vanilla already scales damage by speed, so a spent arrow hits softer on its own.
betterarrows.config.debugLogging: Write debug info to the log
betterarrows.config.debugLogging.tooltip: Prints which body part each arrow attached to, and any it gave up on. Only needed if arrows show up in the wrong place or not at all - an arrow the mod cannot place is simply invisible, so those two look identical without this. Turn it on, fire a few shots, read latest.log. Leave it off for normal play.
betterarrows.config.iceSlideAngle.toolti: Measured from the SURFACE, like the ricochet angle above: 0 is flat along the ice, 90 is straight down into it. Shots steeper than this bite in and stick, because ice is hard and a square-on arrow should embed rather than skate.
betterarrows.config.iceSlide.tooltip: A shallow shot at ice keeps going ALONG it instead of springing off, and slows down as it goes. Ice reports itself as glass to the game, which is why without this an arrow pings off a frozen lake like a window. Which blocks count is the block tag betterarrows:arrows_slide_on, #minecraft:ice by default - a datapack can add more. Gameplay: needs the mod on the server.
betterarrows.config.iceSlideKept.tooltip: How much speed survives each graze along the ice. High is the point - that is what slippery means - but it cannot reach 100, or the arrow would slide until it left the world.
betterarrows.config.iceSlideMax.tooltip: Hard cap on how many times one arrow may graze ice before it just sticks. Speed loss should stop it long before this - it is a backstop, so no combination of settings can leave an arrow skating across a frozen ocean forever.
betterarrows.config.iceSlideSettle.toolt: How much of the arrow's speed INTO the ice survives each contact. At 0 the slide cancels it entirely, and the arrow leaves the last block of ice falling at exactly nothing - which reads as gliding flat across the water for a dozen blocks. A quarter lets it settle onto the surface and leave the edge already dropping.
betterarrows.config.iceBounce.tooltip: An arrow cannot bury itself in ice, so a shot too steep to skate is thrown off instead. This is the MOST it can keep, at a near-glancing angle; the steeper the hit the less it keeps, and a square-on strike keeps nothing at all and simply drops - that is the one case with no energy left to bounce with.
